result:
I repaired the subject's name and replaced "Muhammad Ali" with "Joe Frazier" as the reparandum. Like Ali, Frazier is a man's name and a famous American boxer, so it is an easy slip to make. No WordNet lookup was needed because only the name changes.

1. **Gold concepts:** 0 `male.n.02` (Name "Muhammad Ali"), 1 `be.v.08`, 2 `time.n.08`, 3 `country.n.02` (Name "america"), 4 `person.n.01`, 5 `boxer.n.01`.
2. **Why the anchor (⑤) is needed:** The repaired concept, `male.n.02` (position 0), has only a name constant and no roles of its own. The only edge into it is `be.v.08 Theme`, which comes after the repair. On its own, the reparandum would not connect to the rest of the sentence (rule R5). So I put an `entity.n.01` anchor before `CORRECTION`. Both men carry `EQU` back to the anchor, and `be.v.08 Theme` now points to the anchor.
3. **Recount in the repaired SBN:** Positions are 0 `entity.n.01`, 1 Joe Frazier, 2 Muhammad Ali, 3 `be.v.08`, 4 `time.n.08`, 5 `country.n.02`, 6 `person.n.01`, 7 `boxer.n.01`.
   - `be.v.08` has `Theme -3` to the anchor, `Time +1` to `time.n.08` and `Co-Theme +3` to `person.n.01`.
   - Inside `person.n.01`, `Source -1` and `Role +1` are unchanged.
   - No separators come after the repair, so no box pointers needed updating.
